summary: Two wooden range towers built 1917-18 to guide ships into the Port Borden ferry harbour; dark since the Confederation Bridge opened in 1997.

light.reflectors: Duplex burners with 20-inch reflectors per LighthouseFriends and the page image of the 1917-18 Marine report (scan p.31, printed p.32, row Port Borden; the OCR text reads 23-inch)

structures.type: square pyramidal wood tower with square lantern
structures.note: Rowlett gives 6.5 m (22 ft); LighthouseFriends gives 6.2 m (22 ft); the Society's technical data give 6.5 m (21 ft 3 in). Stands at its last official site by the shore.

structures.type: square pyramidal wood tower with gallery
structures.note: Rowlett gives 12 m (35 ft); LighthouseFriends gives 12.8 m (42 ft) base to vane; the Society's technical data give 11.6 m (38 ft) tower height and its description 12.8 m (42 ft). Relocated in 1923 and again in 1954-55; now in the Marine/Rail Historical Park.

events.note: Site acquired in 1917. The PEI Lighthouse Society says it was expropriated on 12 February 1917; LighthouseFriends says the government purchased sites for $225.
Range lights built in 1917 (PEI Lighthouse Society: Date Built 1917). The Marine report for 1917-18 records the erection of range lights at Port Borden.
William Carruthers, first keeper of both range lights (LighthouseFriends; PEI Lighthouse Society)
Range lights officially established; LighthouseFriends says originally equipped with 20-inch reflectors and duplex burners
Marine report for fiscal 1920-21 lists a change in the position of range lights at 'Port Bordon'. The entry sits in a list that mixes provinces; the match with these lights is by name only.
Range lights moved in 1923 (Rowlett; PEI Lighthouse Society)
Moved again in 1954-55 as the approach to the ferry dock was modified (Rowlett; PEI Lighthouse Society)
Decommissioned in June 1997 when the Confederation Bridge opened and ferry service ended

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Society gives 1917 for the build: the site was expropriated on 12 February 1917 and the range light built later that year. The Marine report for 1917-18 records the erection in that fiscal year. LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1918, which matches the official establishment. The story gives both: built 1917, established 1918.

The OCR of the 1917-18 Marine report reads 23-inch reflectors. The page image (scan p.31, printed p.32), row Port Borden, reads 20-inch, which matches LighthouseFriends. Resolved in favour of 20-inch; the story no longer repeats the OCR figure.

notes_for_editor: 1) Reflector size: resolved from the page image (scan p.31, printed p.32). The row Port Borden reads 20-inch reflectors with duplex burners, and the cost 1,204.97; the OCR text misreads the figure as 23-inch. This matches LighthouseFriends. 2) Heights: Rowlett gives the front 6.5 m and LighthouseFriends 6.2 m (both 22 ft); the Society's technical data give 6.5 m (21 ft 3 in) front and 11.6 m (38 ft) rear, while its description gives 12.8 m (42 ft). The story states the spread. 3) Record focal_height_m 23.0 and characteristic 'F Y' (Wikidata-derived) could not be confirmed from any source read here. Not used. 4) Ferry origin: Rowlett's Cape Jourimane against LighthouseFriends and the PEI Society's Cape Tormentine. The story states the disagreement. 5) Front tower condition: PEI Society says restored; LighthouseFriends says abandoned and neglected; Rowlett says endangered by erosion (2012 repaint). Stated in the text, not resolved. 6) Keepers: no primary keeper record was found. The corpus Marine reports (to 1924) do not list a Port Borden range keeper. Carruthers rests on LighthouseFriends and the Society; McDonald on LighthouseFriends alone. 7) 'Port Bordon' (FY1920-21, scan p.33): the entry sits in a list of changes to existing aids that mixes provinces, and the printed name is hard to read in the page image. The match is by name only. 8) Do not confuse with Port Borden Pier light (CCG list, H1039, the ferry pier light at Borden-Carleton, a different structure). 9) Record's rear location (46.250057, -63.705076) and LighthouseFriends' (46.24979, -63.70517) agree within about 60 m. 10) The record's status 'inactive' is correct. No correction proposed. 11) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the reflector size was checked in the page image; the Marine FY1917-18 entry and the Tuplin-style row alignment were checked there as well.
